milestone: Runtime integer shape lists for flat-array CPU tensor construction
implementation: ArrayToTensor has optional explicit dimension operands: absence preserves rank-one construction, an empty list constructs rank zero. The source shape list fixes rank while dimensions are ordinary completed integer scalars. Semantic analysis preserves known extents/count constraints and refines fixed expected extents into pre-allocation checks. CPU lowering evaluates dimension expressions before shape validation, guards integer ranges, byte products and row-major suffix strides, checks input length, then copies flat input into ranked indices. Continuation kernels and imported callback/helper graphs remap all dimension operands. Existing scalar/constant-ranked literal construction and numeric engines/checked ABI/runtime are unchanged.

contract.syntax: tensor(values,[rows,columns]); flat numeric literal data also accepts runtime dimensions. tensor(values) and existing constant-shaped literals retain their behavior.
contract.types: Six numeric CPU data types and four completed integer dimension types (int32,uint32,int64,uint64), including mixed integer widths/signs. No implicit data element conversion.
contract.rank: Rank fixed by a source list, values dynamic. [] requires one element; zero dimensions require empty data. Unknown-rank shape-array variables, inferred -1 dimensions and tensor-to-tensor reshape remain outside this slice.
contract.validation: Known count/extent contradictions rejected. Runtime dimensions fit nonnegative int64 indexing, expected extents match, byte products and row-major suffix strides fit, and input length equals shape product before allocation. Empty shapes still require valid strides.
contract.failures: Dimension/rank/count constraints yield Shape faults; byte/stride overflow yields Allocation faults. Ordinary integer expression faults keep original locations. Dimension expressions evaluate once in source order before constructor validation. No partial output or retained-owner leaks on failure/cancellation.
contract.ownership: Checked row-major copies preserve raw bits and borrowed input. Retained tensor output survives input mutation/settlement and worker exit. Direct/nested workers and cached awaits reuse existing layouts/ownership.
contract.scope: CPU flat-array construction with explicit shapes, including matrices. No GPU/mixed-target construction or distributed implementation.

qualification.scope: Focused reshape, prior array constructors, tensor inference, numeric/collection/frontend, source/tasks/recovery, storage and selected Metal regressions; not full suite.
coverage: 24 element/dimension type pairs checked and lowered; optional dimension operands preserve rank and concrete data identity.
Rank-two raw copies for all six data types; ranks zero/one/three for int64 and float32; uint64 and mixed int32/uint32 dimensions; fixed rank-two expected extents.

Boundary/random raw bits (signed zero, subnormals, infinities, NaN payloads), eight ARM FP states, strided borrowed inputs, exact row-major indices, allocation failure and retained outputs after source mutation/settlement.

Negative and oversized unsigned dimensions; mismatched counts; byte-count overflow; row-major stride overflow with a leading zero; representable large zero-suffix shapes; high-bit uint32 zero-element shapes.
Fixed extents validated before allocation; source locations preserved, output descriptors absent on error and all invocation owners settled.
Active million-element copy cancellation and pre-entry cancellation for six rank-two numeric families, including checked partial-copy cleanup.
Direct and nested matrix workers, constructor inside imported nested anonymous callbacks, mixed-width dimension captures, cached awaits and retained matrix result layouts.
Six numeric matrix multiplication/reduction results after worker construction, plus flat-literal/runtime-dimension and rank-zero/rank-three direct worker programs.
1/2/4-worker success/cancellation/deadline/admission; core allocation failure positions 1-8 and generated invocation failure positions 1-8 with two workers; supervised Arithmetic/Shape recovery.
Both faulting dimension-call orders and argument-before-validation order preserve first Arithmetic source and clean all intermediate owners.
Invalid count/noninteger/unknown-rank shape programs preserve existing output artifacts. Malformed dimension IDs/types/ranks rejected before lowering.
Debug, optimized, ASan/UBSan and separate ThreadSanitizer execution, sanitized frontend and earlier constructor/inference/numeric/source/storage/selected GPU regressions.

remaining_gates: Tensor-to-tensor reshape, inferred dimensions and runtime-variable rank
Tensor-to-array construction, broader value types and modules
Native distributed execution requires design discussion
